title: Zeroth homology of the canonical right-derived single augmentation
statement: Let C,D be abelian categories with derived categories, enough injectives and K-injective resolutions in C, and let F:C→D be additive and left exact. The canonical natural map single(FM)→RF(single M), formed by the inverse termwise-single comparison and the right-derived unit, has zeroth homology inverse to the canonical composite H⁰(RF(single M))≅R⁰F(M)≅F(M). Thus composing its H⁰ map with that isomorphism gives the canonical single/H⁰ isomorphism. The same statement remains true after any exact additive functor D→E, using its homology comparison. For additive left exact R:C→D and T:C→E and exact additive S:D→E, write v for the single comparison inverse followed by S_D of the R-augmentation, and w for the T-augmentation. If f:S_D(RR(X[0]))→RT(X[0]) and c:S(RX)→TX satisfy v≫f=single_E(c)≫w, conjugating H⁰(f) by the two canonical H⁰ identifications gives c.

proof.text: Compare the total right-derived unit with the bounded-below right-derived unit by the uniqueness factorization. Naturality of that unit on an injective-resolution augmentation identifies its homology with the classical augmentation to R⁰F. The single comparison cancels its chain-level single-map inverse. Left exactness identifies toRightDerivedZero with inverse to rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf. The exact-postcomposition variant follows by naturality of the exact homology comparison and its single-object formula.

Apply zeroth homology to any augmentation-compatible square. The two augmentation calculations identify its vertical maps, after the canonical H⁰ isomorphisms, with the single/homology isomorphisms. Cancel these isomorphisms and use their naturality to identify the normalized map with the ordinary map.
